summary: Thomas Zehnder works in Indology and linguistics. He completed his PhD at the University of Zurich and studied under Alexander Lubotsky from 1997 to 1998.

Thomé H. Fang (1899–1977) was a scholar of philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He held academic posts at National Central University (around 1929–1948) and National Taiwan University (around 1948–1973).
Thongchai Winichakul is a historian who studied at Thammasat University from around 1973 to 1981. He held a post at the University of Wisconsin–Madison from around 1991 to 2016.

Thubten Yeshe (1935–1984) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Sera Monastery and under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and Trijang Rinpoche. In 1982, he held posts at Middlebury College and the University of Virginia.
Thubten Zopa Rinpoche (1946–2023) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Thubten Yeshe, Trijang Rinpoche, and Denma Lochö Rinpoche, and he co-founded Kopan Monastery in 1971.

Thupten Jinpa is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who studied at Ganden Shartse Monastery and the University of Cambridge. He held posts at Ganden Shartse, Girton College, Cambridge, and the Institute of Tibetan Classics.

Théodore Pavie (1811–1896) was an Indologist and Sinologist who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He later served as Professor of Sanskrit at the Collège de France (1852–1857) and held a post at the Catholic University of the West around 1877.

Thích Minh Châu (1918–2012) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar Bihar University and served as a lecturer in Chinese at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara from around 1957 to 1964.

Thích Thiện Châu (1931–1998) was a scholar in the field of Buddhist studies. He pursued his education in France, studying at Paris-Sorbonne University from around 1967 to 1971 and at Sorbonne Nouvelle University from around 1971 to 1977.

Tianshu Zhu works in archaeology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Northwest University (MA) and Ohio State University (PhD under John C. Huntington), Zhu held positions at Shaanxi History Museum, Northwest University, Ohio State University, and Korea University.

Tilak Kariyawasam is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served as head of the Department of Pali and Buddhist Studies at the University of Kelaniya and as Dean of the Graduate School at the International Buddhist College.

Tilmann Vetter (1937–2012) specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Vienna under Erich Frauwallner and Erich Heintel, later holding posts at Utrecht University (~1967–1973) and Leiden University (from 1974).

Tim Dean studied at the University of East Anglia under Robert Clark, Brandeis University, and Johns Hopkins University. He has held academic posts at the University of Washington, the University at Buffalo, and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.
Tim Stowell is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology from around 1976 to 1981. He took up a post at the University of California, Los Angeles around 1982.

Timothy Brook is a Sinologist and historian who studied at the University of Toronto and Harvard University. He held academic posts at the University of Toronto, the University of British Columbia, and the Institute for Advanced Study.

Timothy H. Barrett is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Cambridge and Yale, taught at the University of Cambridge from around 1975 to 1986, and became a professor at SOAS in 1986.
Timothy Lenz is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Washington under Richard Salomon and Collett Cox, and he later became a professor there.

Timothy Lubin is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed his PhD at Columbia University around 1987–1994. He held an academic post at Washington and Lee University starting around 2000.

Tina Rasmussen is a scholar in the fields of Buddhist studies and religious studies. She studied under traditional teacher Pa-Auk Sayadaw from around 2005 to 2006 and completed her MA under the supervision of Christian K. Wedemeyer.

Tissa Rajapatirana is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong. He subsequently held a post at ANU from around 1968 to 1998.
